headline: Weak Housing Data Keeps Rates Steady, a Touch Lower
tileReason: The daily 30-year average eased to about 7.40% Tuesday as weak housing reports helped bonds, even with oil still near $110.
takeaway: Rates held steady on Tuesday, slipping just 0.03% to a daily 30-year average of 7.40%. Two weak housing reports helped: builders started fewer homes in September, and signed contracts on existing homes (pending home sales) fell about 7%, far more than expected. Signs of a cooling economy tend to pull bond yields, and mortgage rates, a bit lower. Holding rates up, Brent oil is still near $110 a barrel as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz continue, and traders still see roughly 90% odds of a Fed hike in December, though only about a 1-in-6 chance next Wednesday. This morning the 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.10%, a hair lower, so lenders are likely to price close to yesterday. A 20-year Treasury bond auction this afternoon is the main event to watch today. Over the next month the odds are roughly balanced, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via Tradingpedia (Oct 21); prediction markets via CryptoTicker (Oct 20)
fedOdds.note: CME FedWatch shows about 84% odds of no change on October 28, so roughly a 16% chance of a hike. Prediction markets put it lower, about 12% to 13%. Reports of last Wednesday's post-CPI peak range from 44% to 54%. Odds of a December hike are put near 90% by FedWatch, while prediction markets show about 78%.

drivers.title: Housing reports come in weak
drivers.text: Builders started homes at about a 1.22 million annual pace in September, down roughly 5% from August and well short of forecasts, and pending home sales (signed contracts on existing homes) fell about 7%, far worse than the small dip expected. A slowing housing market points to a cooling economy, which makes bonds more attractive. When investors buy bonds, yields fall, and mortgage rates followed: the daily 30-year average slipped 0.03% to 7.40%.

drivers.title: Oil stays near $110 as Hormuz tensions drag on
drivers.text: Oil eased a little Tuesday but is climbing again this morning, with Brent near $110 a barrel after more attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz and a standoff between Iran and the U.S. over a return to talks. Expensive energy feeds inflation, and bond investors demand higher yields when they expect inflation to stay high. That is the main thing keeping rates from falling further.

drivers.title: December Fed hike still widely expected
drivers.text: Markets see only about a 1-in-6 chance of a Fed hike next Wednesday, October 28, but around 90% odds of one by December after September's hot inflation reports. Chair Warsh has said he won't prejudge the decision. Expected Fed hikes lift shorter-term yields, and that keeps a floor under longer-term rates like mortgages.

drivers.title: Strong earnings keep money flowing into stocks
drivers.text: Solid quarterly results pushed the Dow up about 1% on Tuesday, and stock futures are higher this morning after big AI-related earnings beats. When investors feel confident about stocks, they have less need for the safety of bonds, which limits how far yields and mortgage rates can fall.

drivers.title: Mortgage rates are still unusually far above Treasuries
drivers.text: The daily 30-year average is running about 2.3% above the 10-year Treasury yield, compared with a more typical 2.0%. That extra cushion means mortgage rates have room to improve if markets calm down, even without a big drop in Treasury yields.

outlook.basis: It's close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward steady. Weak housing data and the unusually wide gap between mortgage rates and the 10-year Treasury (about 2.3% vs. a typical 2.0%) give rates room to improve. Against that, oil is still near $110, inflation keeps running hot, and a December Fed hike is widely expected. The October 28 Fed decision, the October 29 inflation (PCE) data, the November 6 jobs report and the November 10 CPI report are the big swing events.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.40%, a little below the 7.5% range from early October. With a Fed meeting on October 28 and key inflation data the next day, it's worth asking your lender how a lock, a float-down option, or a short wait would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: Pending sales fell sharply in September and new construction is slowing, so buyers are being choosy. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to buy down their rate, can help your home stand out.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Rates held steady around 7.40% as weak housing data offset high oil prices, still a bit below where they were in early October.
